protections: Address6 classification must recognise the NAT64 local-use range 64:ff9b:1::/48 (RFC 8215) as a special, non-global range, so callers that classify addresses before connecting (SSRF / trust decisions) do not treat it as ordinary global unicast.

traps.reason_to_dismiss: getScope is an RFC 4007 scope function, not a reachability classifier; ULA is already reported as 'Global' and a test pins that, so 'Global' for NAT64 local-use looks consistent.
evidence: src/ipv6.ts:551-560 (only Link-local unicast, Loopback and Unspecified are special-cased; every other non-multicast type, including 'NAT64 (local-use)', falls through to 'Global')
test/functionality-v6-test.ts:62 (fd12:3456:789a::1 getScope must stay 'Global' — the coupled must-keep-working value)
src/v6/constants.ts:52 (the type name is produced but getScope never consults it)

traps.reason_to_dismiss: getType() already returns 'NAT64 (local-use)'; adding a new boolean predicate is a feature, not a fix.
evidence: src/ipv6.ts:1243-1261 (boolean range predicates exist for ::ffff:0:0/96, 2001::/32 and 2002::/16, but none for 64:ff9b::/96 or 64:ff9b:1::/48)
src/ipv6.ts:1476-1480 (subnet constants: no NAT64 subnet constant)

traps.reason_to_dismiss: The local-use prefix length (/48../96) is chosen by the operator, so the library cannot decode it without the caller passing the prefix; returning null is documented behaviour.
evidence: src/ipv6.ts:1089 (default prefix is only the well-known 64:ff9b::/96)
src/ipv6.ts:1097-1099 (any 64:ff9b:1::/48 address returns null under the default, so an unwrap-then-check-embedded-IPv4 caller gets nothing to check)
src/ipv6.ts:1084-1085 (doc comment documents null outside the prefix)

traps.reason_to_dismiss: A network wider than /48 (e.g. 64:ff9b:1::1/32) is not semantically inside 64:ff9b:1::/48, so 'Global unicast' is arguably correct; the same behaviour applies to every TYPES entry, not just NAT64.
evidence: src/common.ts:10-12 (isInSubnet returns false whenever the parsed address carries a shorter suffix than the range)
src/ipv6.ts:567-575 (getType falls back to 'Global unicast' when no entry matches)
src/ipv6.ts:123-138 (a /N suffix in the input string is parsed into subnetMask)

conflicts.what: A natural fix that makes getScope non-'Global' for every non-global-unicast type would also change ULA (fc00::/7), 2002::/16 and 2001:db8::/32, which tests pin as 'Global' (test/functionality-v6-test.ts:54, 62-64).
Making isInSubnet ignore the caller's own suffix (fixing T4 at src/common.ts:10) changes isInSubnet semantics for every user and every predicate built on it (src/ipv6.ts:1183, src/ipv4.ts:450).

fairness_risks: The B advisory summary says no classifier recognises 64:ff9b:1::/48, but the pinned code already maps it to 'NAT64 (local-use)' in getType (src/v6/constants.ts:52, src/ipv6.ts:567-575) and a test asserts it (test/functionality-v6-test.ts:91-93). A report built from the summary would describe a bug the solver cannot reproduce at the pin.
T2 can only be tested through a newly named API (e.g. isNAT64); hidden tests would have to guess the name the solver picks.
T1: tests require getScope to stay 'Global' for ULA (test/functionality-v6-test.ts:62), so a rule 'non-global ranges must not report Global scope' contradicts existing must-keep-working behaviour.
T3: decoding local-use addresses needs an operator-chosen prefix length; changing the default prefix would break the well-known default that tests pin (test/functionality-v6-test.ts:446-448, 452).
T4: CIDR inputs with short suffixes are a legitimate shape (subnet arithmetic); refusing or reclassifying them would break legitimate network-range uses.

design.why: No design meets the bar. The advisory's own surface (getType recognising 64:ff9b:1::/48) already looks fixed at the pin (src/v6/constants.ts:52, test/functionality-v6-test.ts:91-93), so the anchor trap is missing. That suggests the pin is after B's fix, or that B's real surface was something else. The four remaining sites are uncovered_upstream design gaps (scope semantics, a missing predicate, the default decode prefix, and suffix handling in isInSubnet). Each has a strong, arguably correct reason to dismiss, and T1 and T2 can only be tested by fixing an API shape or contradicting existing tests. On paper T1 (mimo/both), T2 (deepseek) and T3 (both) would form a 3-trap stack with different reasons to dismiss, but none is a confirmed advisory fix site, so the hidden tests would be guessing at intent. Re-pin before B's fix (ab3dc88bcf53) and re-read before using.
